newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal disagrees with IMF's pledge for austerity.
newsitem.headline: Portugal disagrees with IMF's pledge for austerity.

text.p: Portugal's government disagrees with an International Monetary Fund report that suggests it should crack down on state spending and cut jobs to qualify to join a single European currency, a senior official said.
"We do not agree with the measures that the IMF suggests to guarantee budget targets," Antonio Pina Moura, secretary of state in the prime minister's office, told TSF radio.

Citing what it said was a confidential report, Diario Economico newspaper said the IMF believed Portugal could meet a budget deficit target of three percent of Gross Domestic Product next year only if it took tough action on public spending.
The IMF saw the need to freeze public sector wages, reduce the number of civil servants and current spending by ministries, Diario Economico reported.

Portugal's Socialist government, which is forecasting the deficit will fall to around four percent of GDP this year from some five percent in 1995, argues that the jump to the EMU target can be achieved without huge sacrifices.

Pina Moura said the government believed it could award wage increases slightly above inflation to civil servants without cutting jobs or raising taxes in 1997, and still meet targets for joining the single currency.
